comment: The calls of a page. x-air-app/toolsCall of the page link is tools/call of the app link with the origin and the view of the connection. air-ide forwards each message of an app through one ordered executor, so a WebSocket gets the frames of a call in the order that the app wrote them.
The setup: the fixture app with Always Allow, the instance main:1 of the tool window, the process up, and one ticket for main:1.

text:
format: 1
id: fixture
name: Fixture
server:
  command: ${dir}/fixture-app
  args: [serve]
views:
  main: { resource: ui://fixture/main, place: toolWindow, toolWindow: { title: Fixture, tabTitle: Overview, titleActions: [refresh] } }
  log: { resource: ui://fixture/log, place: toolWindowTab, toolWindowTab: { of: main, title: Log } }
  review: { resource: ui://fixture/review, place: editor, instances: many }
  settings: { resource: ui://fixture/settings, place: window, window: { width: 880, height: 640 } }
actions:
  - id: refresh
    text: Refresh Fixture
    icon: AllIcons.Actions.Refresh
    groups: [Vcs.MainMenu]
    run: { tool: refresh }

params.message: The app fixture started: pid none, consent allowed, source user

tools.name: invoke
tools.description: Runs one command of the page.

tools.name: summary
tools.description: Summarizes the fixture for an agent.

comment: A call that changes state: the change of the mirror, the events and the call events that the app writes before its answer reach the page before the answer. callId is the id of the call on each link, and progress names the request of the page. An event, a call event and a progress are notices of the app link channel x-air-ide:/appLink/<n> of the process, which no page subscribes to.
An event that names an instance that is not open, such as review:9, reaches no page, and the apps channel logs one warning.
A result passes through as the app wrote it, bytes in base64 too. A call event after the answer of its call is dropped with a log entry.

A cancel of the page is a notification of the root channel. air-ide serves it at once, never behind the call that it cancels: it sends notifications/cancelled to the app and answers the call. The call gets exactly one answer, so the late answer of the app and a second cancel are dropped. Air never sends a call again.
resources/read of a page reads a resource of its own app. Each file of a page of several files is a resource of the app.
A tool with the prefix air_ is a tool of the IDE. air-ide asks the IDE with the app and the instance, and the app never sees it.
A tool whose visibility lacks app is refused with modelOnly, and a name with the prefix air_ that is no tool of the IDE with unknownTool. The app and the IDE get no call.
An action of the app file runs its tool with the origin action, a tool that only the app sees (visibility app) too. The echo comes when the call starts, and a failed call is an IDE notification.

An action in the title of a tool window runs with the instance of that tool window, so the call names the action, its view and its instance. The IDE reports the show of the tool window by appPlace before its first action, so the app hears viewShown before the call. The echo names the instance that the place shows, and the action runs with it.
The proxy air_app of a session calls with the origin agent. An app whose file says agent.tools none refuses every agent call.

The holder sends a click of a view of the Session View with the origin click. A click needs no agent.tools model and no agent consent. The app gets the session block of the view, which the reader of the views gives, and the answer names no UI for a tool without a UI resource.
An error that the app answers reaches the IDE as appError, with the code and the message of the app. No field of the data of the app passes, so the app cannot name the consent request of another app.

air-ide checks the arguments of a tool of the IDE before the IDE gets the call. A bad argument gets an error result that names it, and the IDE gets no call. A root out of the project gets a text that names no path.

content.text: air_open_file needs a line that is an integer.
air_navigate needs a column that is an integer.
air_show_commit needs a root that is a path.
air_show_commit needs a root in the project.
air_show_commit needs a root in the project.

comment: air-ide resolves a relative path and a relative root from the project directory and normalizes them. The IDE gets the absolute path and only the fields of the tool.

An editor tab reports what the IDE shows of it by appPlace, with the key of its tab and the params of its path. air-ide creates the instance of a shown tab without one, once, so a tab that the platform restored after a restart gets its instance. The app hears viewShown and viewHidden once for each change of the select, in the order of the reports, and viewClosed at the close of the tab.
An editor tab whose instance the app closed keeps that instance until its close: it asks for no other one, also after a hide and a show, and its close reports viewClosed of that instance.

The app closes the instance of a tool window. The app hears viewClosed at once, because the content stays, and the place of the tool window counts one hide more, so the IDE hides the tool window. The shown content asks for no new instance until its hide, so a title action then runs without an instance. The next show creates a new instance, and the title action reports the show first and runs with the instance that the echo names.

A tab of a tool window gets its instance at its first show, and the content of the view hides. A frame names a view of one instance by the id of the view as its key, so it finds the instance that the app opened.

A report that does not fit the app file is refused: a view that it does not declare, another place than its place, a key of a content of a tool window, an editor tab without its key, and params of a frame.

The app closes the instance of a place and opens a new instance of the same key before the IDE closes the place. The close of the place closes only the instance that it showed, so the app hears viewClosed of the instance that it closed, and the new instance stays. The place of the new instance then shows it, and the app hears viewShown. An editor tab gets no other instance at its show.

A close of a place names the instance that the IDE showed in it, and it closes no other instance. The user closes the tab of review:10. Then the user closes a restored tab while its show waits for the bind of the apps channel. The show does not go, and the close names no instance: air-ide knows no place and no open instance of the key, so the close closes nothing. The app then opens review:11 of the key. A close that names review:10 comes for the place of the key, which air-ide does not know, as from a second window of the file or after a new bind: review:11 stays, and the next tab of the key shows it. Only a close names an instance.
